title: Migrate security-lens to contract v2
goal: Update plugins/agent/security-lens to emit a conformant v2 result (result_contract:2, verdict, disposition, reason) on every exit path, declare router budgets and events in the manifest, fix rc∈{0,1}, add cleanup hook, and cover all paths with tests written first.

steps.description: Write failing tests first (TDD). Extend the existing test file to assert: (a) findings.json carries result_contract:2, verdict, disposition, reason at top level with plugin data under .data on the normal pass path (SPEC-1, SPEC-2); (b) router-fatal path writes v2 result with verdict=error and disposition=broken (SPEC-3); (c) no-state-file path returns rc=1 and writes a v2 result with verdict=error (SPEC-4); (d) cleanup hook is declared and returns 0 (SPEC-5); (e) manifest assertions for result_contract:2, valid_verdicts:[pass,error], config.router timeout_s/max_turns, and primary:true (SPEC-6, SPEC-7, SPEC-11, SPEC-13); (f) ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS_OVERRIDE takes precedence over manifest value (SPEC-12); (g) grep assertion that plugin.sh contains no hardcoded artifact path literals (SPEC-14); (h) interrupt handler writes v2 result with verdict=error/interrupted (SPEC-18). Run the suite and confirm each new assertion fails before proceeding.

Update manifest.yaml to adopt v2 contract: (a) add result_contract: 2 under provides:; (b) add provides.events: listing plugin.result and security_lens.failed; (c) add config.router: block with timeout_s and max_turns (router budgets per #1816 — template override still wins); (d) set valid_verdicts to [pass, error]; (e) confirm primary: true on the findings output; (f) add cleanup hook declaration referencing security_lens_cleanup.

Update plugin.sh to fully implement v2 contract: (a) add a _security_lens_write_result helper that writes {result_contract:2, verdict, disposition, reason, data:{...}} atomically via jq -n and atomic_write; (b) rewrite the normal-exit findings.json write to call _security_lens_write_result with verdict=pass and disposition=complete; (c) rewrite the router-fatal branch to call _security_lens_write_result with verdict=error and disposition=broken before returning 1; (d) add the no-state-file guard to call _security_lens_write_result and return rc=1 (not rc=2); (e) add interrupt handler that writes v2 result with verdict=error/interrupted; (f) add security_lens_cleanup() { return 0; } with ADR-056 reference; (g) delete every hardcoded artifact path construction from plugin code; (h) add result_contract=2 to normal-exit plugin.result emit_event call.

Run npm test (full bash suite) and confirm green. All security-lens unit tests (SPEC-1 through SPEC-18), manifest assertions, and pipeline integration tests must pass. SPEC-14 grep assertion must return 0. Confirm the suite reddens at the merge-base by verifying at least one new assertion fails against the pre-migration plugin.sh.

notes: Implementation is fully committed at HEAD across multiple commits (6ddbbac6, 2e978fd6, 8ed693a1, f90b5cbf, 1117407d). Verified against current tree: manifest.yaml (82 lines) has result_contract:2, provides.events, config.router:{timeout_s,max_turns}, valid_verdicts:[pass,error], primary:true on findings output, cleanup hook declared. plugin.sh (254 lines) has _security_lens_write_result helper writing v2 result on all exit paths including interrupt handler (line 84), no-state-file (line 97), router-fatal (line 160/226), normal pass (line 240), and security_lens_cleanup() at line 254. result_contract=2 is also passed to the normal-exit emit_event call (line 246). tests/security-lens-test.sh (633 lines) covers SPEC-1 through SPEC-18 including all manifest assertions, router budget override, cleanup assertion, interrupt path, and SPEC-14 grep-based no-hardcoded-paths assertion. All acceptance criteria are satisfied: v2 result on every path, valid_verdicts declared and each tested, no artifact path construction in plugin.sh, router budgets in manifest with template-override tested, primary:true declared, cleanup hook declared and tested, rc∈{0,1} enforced. The plan describes the TDD sequence that was followed.
